card.name: Khorumi
card.profile: Khorumi is a war dance originating in Adjara (sometimes attributed to neighbouring Guria) in southwestern Georgia, rooted in the country's many invasions (Wikipedia; geofolk.ge). Originally performed by only a few men, today's version sees thirty or forty dancers participate, with the rules requiring the number to be odd. It has four parts: searching for a campsite, reconnoitering the enemy camp, the fight, and the victory celebration. Unusually, it is accompanied only by instruments - the doli (drum) and chiboni (bagpipe) - never by clapping, and uses a distinctive five-beat (3+2) meter. Some scholars link it to dances of ancient Georgian tribes described by Xenophon.
card.insight: Khorumi was named a Monument of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Georgia in 2013 and has become a template for the performance of Georgian military skill; in 2024-25 it was adopted by pro-EU protesters in Tbilisi as a dance of peaceful resistance (Georgia Today; geofolk.ge).
